claims.summary: Any unsatisfiable Boolean graph-constraint system with one variable per edge of a simple n>=3 vertex graph and multilinear constraints local to vertex stars has PC degree <=ceil((m-a)b/(2(b-1))+Delta sqrt(8b log(2b)))+2Delta over any field, for a matching of size a and b=n-a. After isolated vertices are handled, maximal matching gives (1/2-1/(4Delta-2))m+O_Delta(sqrt(m log m)) for fixed Delta, and m/2-Omega(m/log m) for Delta=O(log m).
claims.assessment: Working complete ordinary-PC proof. Local predicates give forbidden assignment indicators through2Delta; frontier elimination reuses derived indicators within bags of size cutwidth+Delta. Independent matched-block keys, cut Lipschitz bound4Delta, and a union bound give the ordering. Exact local checks over F2/F3 cover all two-relation cases; the asymptotic proof is analytic. No polynomial proof-size bound or arbitrary bounded-width CNF extension is claimed.
claims.rationale: A general upper-degree calibration excludes bounded-degree graph constraint families from the moving midpoint sufficient route. The construction is elementary frontier elimination plus a matching-based ordering; no novelty or Frege upper bound is claimed.

claims.summary: Canonical forbidden-assignment CNF encodings of positive integer-flow constraints on graphs, with polynomial encoding length in m Boolean edge variables, have PC refutation degree <=m/2-Omega(m/log m). They cannot meet the moving old-degree hypothesis at approximation depth ell>=3. Fixed maximum degree also excludes the depth2 window; growing-degree depth2 and noncanonical encodings are not settled.
claims.assessment: Working corollary over every field after Boolean predicate encoding. Net flows sum to zero, so constraints are unsatisfiable; at least half local assignments are forbidden, forcing Delta=O(log m) under polynomial canonical encoding length. The bound includes both the frontier cost and the original local conversion reserve. No Frege proof-size conclusion follows.
claims.rationale: Settles the current fixed-degree flow candidate and a logarithmic-degree canonical regime for the sufficient old-window approach. It does not close the unrestricted hard-family question or the main lower-bound goal.

relationships: Adapts the independent-key ordering argument to matched vertex blocks; no character or modular constraint is used in the new frontier elimination.
Canonical flow predicates fit the graph-local Boolean model and polynomial encoding length forces logarithmic maximum degree.
The actual PC upper degree lies below the required near-half-variable cutoff in the specified depth regimes; no claim that this sufficient window is necessary for all architectures.
The prior modular argument did not apply to positive flow; the new generic frontier proof resolves that candidate without a fixed-character hypothesis.
